chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The body is built upon bread.

key_terms.إِنَّمَا: Only / Rather, indicating exclusivity or emphasis
key_terms.الْجَسَدُ: The body, referring to the physical form

ai.seo_question: What is the primary food that sustains the human body according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies bread as the foundational sustenance of the human body, reflecting the pre-modern understanding of diet where grain was the primary caloric source. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on moderation and the recognition of food as a divine trust (*amanah*) necessary for physical survival, linking bodily needs to spiritual discipline. It serves as a practical reminder that while the body is hollow and requires constant replenishment, its maintenance should not distract from higher spiritual pursuits.
